A1.justification: Both complete 48-page PDFs describe CURIE and include Appendices A–F. Pages 2–48 have identical extracted text and rendered appearance; page 1 differs only in authorship, author-line layout, and the arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v1 reports original CURIE model evaluations, quantitative comparisons, and expert assessments in Section 5, Tables 1–2, and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original CURIE evaluation results, including model comparisons, expert assessments, ablations, and task-specific analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark procedures and proposed evaluators are unchanged, including LLMSim dictionary matching in Section 4.3 and the probability-weighted LMScore in Appendix D.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same ten tasks across six scientific domains, with identical dataset statistics in Appendix A and task variants in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical within each reported experiment. The open- and closed-model comparisons in Tables 1–2 and 5–7 contain no added, removed, or revised comparison methods.

E3.justification: The prompting procedures, input preparation, evaluation metrics, sample sizes, and human evaluation protocols in Section 4 and the appendices are identical.

E4.justification: The MPV ablations in Table 2, difficulty analysis in Figure 7, and Appendix F analyses—including BIOGR modality ablations and PDB sequence-length effects—are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical, including the single-run statement in Section 4.1, quartile error-bar descriptions, and the three-run BIOGR analysis in Appendix F.6.3.

E6.justification: All numerical results, plotted findings, and qualitative examples match across versions, including main Tables 1–2 and appendix Tables 5–7. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The LLMSim matching and precision/recall/F1 definitions in Section 4.3 and the LMScore equation in Appendix D are identical. No mathematical assumptions, reasoning, or derivations change.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about the 580-example, ten-task benchmark, model-based evaluation contributions, and challenges facing existing LLMs.

C2.justification: Section 6 and Appendix F retain the same interpretations of model behavior. Appendix E preserves the limitations concerning benchmark scale, automated evaluation, prompting coverage, and obtaining human performance.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement, code/data access links, prompts, annotation procedures, and evaluation implementation details are identical. Embedded link targets also match.

R1.justification: Section 2, citations, and the reference list are unchanged. The paper's positioning relative to scientific NLP and long-context benchmarks remains identical.

P1.justification: v2 adds Ekin Dogus Cubuk, Muratahan Aykol, and Amil Merchant to the author list and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. The body wording and document structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded author list changes line wrapping on page 1. All figures, tables, captions, and the layout of pages 2–48 remain visually identical.

improvement.justification: The revision changes author attribution and the version stamp, with limited author-line reflow. Scientific content, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations, and reproducibility information—including all appendices—are identical, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
